card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our wedding cake's gone: theft, accident, or the dog. I suspect theft.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on him. Get him outside before Mum sees.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. I'll take him; check under the table for crumbs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That icing's from yesterday. The crumbs lead into the cloakroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Theft leads again. Keep the dog here; let's see whether that trail ends at a dropped cake or somebody's coat.

mechanism: A names competing cake explanations and changes the leading theory as icing and crumbs alter their relative plausibility.
confusable: Unlike clinging to one clue or one suspicion, A must preserve multiple possible accounts and visibly switch allegiance.
comparison: The cake alternative shifts between theft and dog involvement and proposes following a trail; the hall alternative moves from wiring to economy to weather.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
